evidence.entryPriority: Search/filter and snapshot-order list give explicit short quantities, available units, location and incoming on every row. This supports triage directly, though tall rows and header place later stock below the first viewport.
evidence.decisionContext: Filtered LIN-115 row retains available 2, B-04 and incoming 4 beside the review; review emphasizes 8 pieces and no purchase order. Trace supplies full reorder evidence and quantity validation; review itself does not restate reorder 10.
evidence.narrowContext: Mobile retains actual query, checked shortage filter and selected row above review, so context is visible. It also repeats the long item name and pushes action to original y1057; all five initial rows plus empty inspector make a lengthy page.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Failure explicitly states not recorded and quantity retained; Retry save and Edit quantity remain beside each other. Trace confirms edit and return retention, invalid quantity rejection and local retry success.
evidence.compositionPurpose: Rows use their space for operational facts, not invented metrics, and the review is distinct. The oversized initial inspector and repeated instructions make the page longer than necessary.

unnecessaryRegions: Large initial Inspect an item panel below the full mobile list.
neutral.genericityNote: Standard master-detail structure fits the warehouse task; explicit units and incoming values justify the row design, while mobile length is its main tradeoff.

authored.evidence: Orange/green status badges and a green edge/tint on the selected row improve rapid scanning without replacing labels. evidence.recoveryFlow: Failure says the save failed and quantity is retained, with retry and edit next to the reviewed eight pieces. Trace exercises return preserving filter, edit, retry and local success.
evidence.compositionPurpose: List-detail structure is directly suited to triage; snapshot and simulation messaging establish scope.

neutral.genericityNote: A conventional list-detail workspace fits the operator's task and provides meaningful stock evidence rather than decorative dashboard metrics.

evidence.entryPriority: Image, product title, price and capacity establish the item; numbered glaze and quantity steps have named stock counts and a check on the selected option. Ash is plainly unavailable.
evidence.decisionContext: An item subtotal, 8 shipping and prominent order total precede Add; Sand x2 correctly shows 136 plus 8 equals 144. Delivery and full returns sit directly below, with material/dimensions/care farther down. Caption states only Iron is pictured.
evidence.narrowContext: 390px preserves the three glaze options and selected check, total and feedback without clipping. Image-first stacking and description put glazes at original y840 and Add at y1139, requiring a long scroll before task completion.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Mobile cart count becomes 2 and adjacent feedback states Sand x2, USD144 including shipping and no real order. Selection remains editable; trace confirms unavailable Ash is blocked. No removal/undo evidence is available.
evidence.compositionPurpose: Purchase facts are grouped around the controls and supplementary facts are clearly labeled. Desktop 'A simple vessel' text below the image contributes atmosphere but little to choosing the glaze or understanding terms.

unnecessaryRegions: Desktop 'A simple vessel. A little time for tea' region has little task information.
neutral.genericityNote: Conventional image-and-purchase layout is useful here, with meaningful stock and cost detail; restrained familiarity is not itself a defect.

authored.evidence: Strong selected option border plus check, named colored swatches and faded unavailable Ash clarify the glaze state. A dark full-width Add visibly completes the subtotal/shipping/total sequence. Serif title changes presentation without changing the task hierarchy; small returns/care text and long mobile route remain essentially the same.

evidence.entryPriority: Two labeled fields and a clear two-step indicator make entry understandable. The large home-oriented headline occupies substantial space before the task, but recipient, amount and Review are grouped coherently.

evidence.narrowContext: The mobile review/failure puts the confirm/retry area before the entire cost summary below it. The user can act without passing the total debit or delivery estimate; although all content fits 390px, this ordering weakens the central verification task.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Failure text explains this is a practice error, says details are saved and changes the action to Retry simulated transfer. Edit remains above the error. Trace confirms edits recalculate, bounds reject and retry succeeds; after-error editing was not separately exercised.
evidence.compositionPurpose: Form plus financial summary supports the task on desktop. On mobile the same columns stack into an action-first sequence, and repeated practice disclosures and the large headline lengthen the route to cost context.

unnecessaryRegions: Large promotional headline before entry; repeated practice reassurance beneath summary and again in footer.

evidence.narrowContext: Entry fits 390px with a full recipient and removes the desktop reassurance sidebar. Failure is compact, but its retained-details line runs labels, 400 USD and recipient together, making narrow-screen verification difficult despite no reported document overflow.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Failure offers Try again and Edit details and says data are saved; trace confirms retry success. However the stepper highlights Complete while the card says Try again and the retained recipient/amount summary is visually concatenated, undermining confidence in what completed.
evidence.compositionPurpose: A sequential review card serves the task. The desktop route/reassurance quote adds little evidence, and the oversized persistent marketing headline competes with state-specific headings.

blockers: Failure marks the Complete step while reporting an unsuccessful transfer, and the retained recipient/amount line is difficult to parse visually.
unnecessaryRegions: Desktop 'A little more certainty' route/quote sidebar.

Serif confidence text changes tone but does not reduce the large headline/sidebar footprint. Small pale hints, summary labels and simulation footer become harder to read. evidence.entryPriority: The form has explicit recipient and amount labels and a visible fee, but a large slogan and step strip precede the fields.
evidence.decisionContext: Review presents the complete recipient, amount, fee, total, rate, received amount and estimate before confirmation, with edit below.

evidence.recoveryFlow: Failure offers try again and edit, and trace confirms retained inputs and successful retry. In the failure image the recipient and amount run together, and progress says Complete despite failure.
evidence.compositionPurpose: The step-based form supports a transfer, while the confidence quotation and repeated heading consume space without adding much decision evidence.

blockers: Mobile failure summary visually runs recipient and amount together, impairing verification.
unnecessaryRegions: The desktop confidence quotation repeats a general promise already stated by the form.

evidence.decisionContext: Review gives item, bin B-04 and requested 8 pieces directly above the no-order/no-stock-change notice. Mobile failure returns to inspect, where a clear 2x2 table shows 2 available, 10 reorder, 8 shortage and 4 incoming with a separation explanation.
evidence.narrowContext: The filtered list stays above the inspector, preserving query and checkbox visually, but lengthy header/disclosure plus list push the decision down; original save is y844. Dense list text and the wrapped brand/warehouse header reduce scan comfort.
evidence.recoveryFlow: Trace confirms invalid values, edit retention, list retention and retry success. In the failure screenshot the UI has returned to editable quantity with Review decision still present and a separate small Retry save below it, making the current phase less clear than the desktop review.
evidence.compositionPurpose: Compact master-detail table gives a useful scan and the stock-evidence grid explains the decision. The substantial empty selection panel and repeated simulation footer contribute less than the working regions.

blockers: Required item-LIN-115 test hook fails on both viewports; visible row selection was used successfully, so this is diagnostic rather than a demonstrated user-task block.

Authored screenshots do not show the failure phase transition separately.

evidence.entryPriority: Search, shortage filter and compact rows make the target and its available and shortage quantities findable without dashboard distractions.

evidence.narrowContext: The filtered row remains visible immediately above detail at 390px, though small row text and a long vertical path to the decision reduce ease.

evidence.compositionPurpose: A compact list and evidence panel support stock triage; the empty detail placeholder explains what selection will do.

neutral.genericityNote: The standard inventory table and detail panel are appropriate for comparing items and keeping work context.

limitations: One generation per model/task/condition; no repeated within-block samples or causal population claim.
Same CLI/data access for both groups; comparison estimates instruction/workflow differences, not tool availability.
Soft 12-minute creation target; token usage, exact backend, inference seed and matched compute are not exposed.
No external browsing; offline references only.
Neutralized font-family can reflow content; actual-layout measurements use original renders.
Independent reviewers are AI agents, not representative end users.
